sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: Every game, from rock, paper, scissors, to tennis, to Mario Kart, is a design system.
sentences.zh: 从剪刀石头布到网球，再到《马力欧卡丁车》，每一款游戏都是一套设计系统。

sentences.en: I like to think of game design as a design discipline that is sort of shoulder-to-shoulder with other design fields like graphic design, or architecture, or industrial design.
sentences.zh: 我倾向于将游戏设计视为一门设计学科，它与平面设计、建筑设计或工业设计等其他设计领域并驾齐驱。

sentences.en: This is Eric Zimmerman.
sentences.zh: 这位是埃里克·齐默尔曼。

sentences.en: I work at the NYU Game Center, and I'm actually a professor of game design, if you can believe it.
sentences.zh: 我在纽约大学游戏中心工作，如果你敢相信的话，我其实是一位游戏设计教授。

sentences.en: The raw materials that game designers work with are the rules.
sentences.zh: 游戏设计师所使用的原材料就是规则。

sentences.en: What game designers do, in essence, is create the rules of the game.
sentences.zh: 从本质上讲，游戏设计师的工作就是创造游戏规则。

sentences.en: But when players enter into the system of the game and decide to follow the rules, what results is play.
sentences.zh: 但当玩家进入游戏系统并决定遵守规则时，产生的结果就是“游玩”。

sentences.en: And play is the opposite of rules.
sentences.zh: 而“游玩”与规则恰恰相反。

sentences.en: So while rules are fixed and rigid and logical, play is improvisational and creative and spontaneous.
sentences.zh: 所以，虽然规则是固定、僵化且合乎逻辑的，但“游玩”却是即兴、富有创造力且自发的。

sentences.en: And that's such an amazing, weird, little paradox of games.
sentences.zh: 这就是游戏那般奇妙、怪异又微小的悖论。

sentences.en: The goal of good game design is what Eric calls meaningful play.
sentences.zh: 优秀游戏设计的目标，就是埃里克所说的“有意义的游玩”。

sentences.en: And it's sort of a shorthand for making sure that you're taking care of your players.
sentences.zh: 这其实是一种简略的说法，旨在确保你照顾好了你的玩家。

sentences.en: Ensuring that players stay engaged and that their actions have consequences.
sentences.zh: 确保玩家保持投入，并确保他们的行为会产生后果。

sentences.en: All of that makes sense.
sentences.zh: 这一切都说得通。

sentences.en: That's Blake Eskin.
sentences.zh: 那是布莱克·埃斯金。

sentences.en: He makes the Observatory podcast for Design Observer.
sentences.zh: 他为“设计观察者”制作了《天文台》播客。

sentences.en: But there's one game.
sentences.zh: 但有一款游戏。

sentences.en: It's a really popular one.
sentences.zh: 它非常受欢迎。

sentences.en: And when I play it, I don't feel taken care of as a player.
sentences.zh: 当我玩它的时候，我感觉不到作为玩家被照顾到了。

sentences.en: I feel bored.
sentences.zh: 我感到无聊。

sentences.en: I feel trapped.
sentences.zh: 我感到被困住了。

sentences.en: I feel like it's never going to end.
sentences.zh: 我觉得它永远不会结束。

sentences.en: Here I go.
sentences.zh: 轮到我了。

sentences.en: Monopoly.
sentences.zh: 《大富翁》。

sentences.en: One, two, three, six.
sentences.zh: 一、二、三，六。

sentences.en: Whoa!
sentences.zh: 哇！

sentences.en: I get some money.
sentences.zh: 我拿到了一些钱。

sentences.en: You get some money.
sentences.zh: 你拿到了一些钱。

sentences.en: I get some money.
sentences.zh: 我拿到了一些钱。

sentences.en: You get some money.
sentences.zh: 你拿到了一些钱。

sentences.en: You are a race car, or a hat, or an iron, or a Scotty Dog.
sentences.zh: 你是赛车、帽子、熨斗，或者是苏格兰梗犬。

sentences.en: I'm the hat.
sentences.zh: 我是帽子。

sentences.en: I'm the hat.
sentences.zh: 我是帽子。

sentences.en: You're circling around and around the board.
sentences.zh: 你在棋盘上绕啊绕。

sentences.en: Passing go.
sentences.zh: 经过起点。

sentences.en: Collecting $200.
sentences.zh: 领取200美元。

sentences.en: Buying property.
sentences.zh: 购买房产。

sentences.en: Having to pay when you land on someone else's property.
sentences.zh: 当你停在别人的房产上时，必须付钱。

sentences.en: Building houses.
sentences.zh: 盖房子。

sentences.en: Passing go again.
sentences.zh: 再次经过起点。

sentences.en: Circling again.
sentences.zh: 再次绕圈。

sentences.en: That's usually the critique of Monopoly.
sentences.zh: 这通常就是对《大富翁》的批评。

sentences.en: That it's very, very slow, and long, and it ends up being this very gradual slog where one player gradually survives the others as, you know,
sentences.zh: 它非常、非常缓慢且漫长，最终变成了一种极其缓慢的苦差事，其中一名玩家逐渐熬过其他人，因为你知道，

sentences.en: everyone is bleeded out for money from each other.
sentences.zh: 每个人都在互相榨干对方的钱财。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: No, I hate it.
sentences.zh: 不，我讨厌它。

sentences.en: Here's Louis C.K.
sentences.zh: 这是路易·C·K。

sentences.en: talking about playing the game with his kids.
sentences.zh: 谈论他和孩子们玩这个游戏的情景。

sentences.en: The Monopoly loss is dark.
sentences.zh: 《大富翁》里的失败是很残酷的。

sentences.en: It's dark.
sentences.zh: 很残酷。

sentences.en: It's heavy.
sentences.zh: 很沉重。

sentences.en: When she loses at Monopoly, I gotta look at her little face, and I go, okay, so here's what's gonna happen now, okay?
sentences.zh: 当她在《大富翁》里输了的时候，我得看着她的小脸，然后我说，好吧，现在会发生什么，明白吗？

sentences.en: All your property, everything you have, all the railroads, your houses, all your money, that's mine now.
sentences.zh: 你所有的房产，你拥有的一切，所有的铁路、你的房子、你所有的钱，现在都是我的了。

sentences.en: Monopoly can be slow.
sentences.zh: 《大富翁》可能会很慢。

sentences.en: The losses, as Louis C.K.
sentences.zh: 正如路易·C·K所指出的，

sentences.en: pointed out, can be dark.
sentences.zh: 失败可能会很残酷。

sentences.en: And yet, the game is incredibly popular.
sentences.zh: 然而，这款游戏却极其受欢迎。

sentences.en: It breaks all of these classic rules of good design, but in very interesting ways.
sentences.zh: 它打破了所有这些优秀设计的经典规则，但方式却非常有趣。

sentences.en: When Monopoly was created, it wasn't supposed to teach children to be ruthless capitalists.
sentences.zh: 当《大富翁》被创造出来时，它本意并非教导孩子们成为冷酷的资本家。

sentences.en: In fact, it was just the opposite.
sentences.zh: 事实上，恰恰相反。

sentences.en: It became the embodiment of everything that it originally set out to critique.
sentences.zh: 它最终成为了它最初旨在批判的一切事物的化身。

sentences.en: And I think that's maybe part of the fascination of Monopoly.
sentences.zh: 我认为这或许是《大富翁》魅力的一部分。

sentences.en: Maybe buried inside this capitalist fantasy are somehow the seeds of its opposite, hidden there somewhere within the design.
sentences.zh: 也许在这个资本主义幻想的深处，某种程度上隐藏着其对立面的种子，就藏在设计的某个地方。

sentences.en: The game we call Monopoly goes back to the Gilded Age, a time of great prosperity in America, at least for the Carnegies and the Rockefellers.
sentences.zh: 我们称之为《大富翁》的游戏可以追溯到镀金时代，那是美国一个繁荣昌盛的时期，至少对于卡内基和洛克菲勒家族来说是这样。

sentences.en: The rest of the country was not doing so well.
sentences.zh: 这个国家的其他人过得并不那么好。

sentences.en: Income inequality was growing.
sentences.zh: 收入不平等正在加剧。

sentences.en: But an economist named Henry George thought he had a solution.
sentences.zh: 但一位名叫亨利·乔治的经济学家认为他找到了解决方案。

sentences.en: Henry George proposed a single tax theory, which would completely upend the American capitalist system as we know it.
sentences.zh: 亨利·乔治提出了单一税理论，这将彻底颠覆我们所知的美国资本主义制度。

sentences.en: Land ownership would be abolished.
sentences.zh: 土地所有权将被废除。

sentences.en: Instead, all land would be public property.
sentences.zh: 取而代之的是，所有土地都将成为公共财产。

sentences.en: Individuals and companies would rent land, and that rent would get taxed.
sentences.zh: 个人和公司将租赁土地，而租金将被征税。

sentences.en: And this, in theory, would create an economy where wealth is distributed more fairly.
sentences.zh: 从理论上讲，这将创造一个财富分配更公平的经济体系。

sentences.en: The theory is much more complicated than that, but that's all you're going to get from me.
sentences.zh: 这个理论比这复杂得多，但你从我这里只能了解到这些。

sentences.en: Go listen to Planet Money or something.
sentences.zh: 去听听《金钱星球》之类的节目吧。

sentences.en: This single tax theory gained a lot of followers, including one woman named Lizzie McGee.
sentences.zh: 这个单一税理论获得了许多追随者，其中包括一位名叫莉齐·马吉的女性。

sentences.en: Lizzie McGee was a woman who I considered very before her time.
sentences.zh: 莉齐·马吉是一位我认为非常超前于她那个时代的女性。

sentences.en: That's Mary Pilon, author of The Monopolists, Obsession, Fury, and the Scandal Behind the World's Favorite Board Game, the story that starts with Lizzie McGee.
sentences.zh: 那是玛丽·皮隆，《大富翁：全球最受欢迎棋盘游戏背后的痴迷、愤怒与丑闻》一书的作者，这个故事始于莉齐·马吉。

sentences.en: Lizzie McGee decided to spread the word about single tax theory.
sentences.zh: 莉齐·马吉决定传播单一税理论。

sentences.en: In 1904, she patented a board game that she called the Landlord's Game.
sentences.zh: 1904年，她为一款她称之为《地主游戏》的棋盘游戏申请了专利。

sentences.en: Landlords at the time were considered to be bad people.
sentences.zh: 当时的房东被认为是坏人。

sentences.en: McGee took a white square board, labeled one corner go to jail, another one she labeled public park.
sentences.zh: 马吉拿了一个白色方形棋盘，在一个角落标注“进监狱”，另一个角落标注“公共公园”。

sentences.en: And the rest of it was rimmed with rectangular spaces that players could rent or buy.
sentences.zh: 其余部分则环绕着玩家可以租赁或购买的矩形空间。

sentences.en: There were no colors, no graphics, just black rectangles and writing on a white board.
sentences.zh: 没有颜色，没有图形，只有白色棋盘上的黑色矩形和文字。

sentences.en: Players rolled dice and circled the board, buying up properties and railroads, collecting money and paying rent.
sentences.zh: 玩家掷骰子绕着棋盘走，购买房产和铁路，收取金钱并支付租金。

sentences.en: Players who ran out of money were sent to the poorhouse.
sentences.zh: 钱花光的玩家会被送进贫民收容所。

sentences.en: Players who trespassed on land were sent to jail.
sentences.zh: 擅自闯入土地的玩家会被送进监狱。

sentences.en: And she created two rule sets.
sentences.zh: 她创建了两套规则。

sentences.en: There was a monopolist rule set and then a single tax rule set.
sentences.zh: 一套是垄断规则，另一套是单一税规则。

sentences.en: If you played with the single tax rules, when one player develops property, everyone benefits.
sentences.zh: 如果你用单一税规则玩，当一名玩家开发房产时，每个人都会受益。

sentences.en: But in the monopolist rules, the goal was to create monopolies and crush each other.
sentences.zh: 但在垄断规则中，目标是建立垄断并互相碾压。

sentences.en: The hope was you'd play with both sets of rules, see the differences, and come away totally sold on the single tax theory.
sentences.zh: 她的希望是你能用这两套规则玩，看看其中的差异，并完全信服单一税理论。

sentences.en: The more vice-laden one clearly has taken off, ironically enough.
sentences.zh: 讽刺的是，充满恶意的那个版本显然更受欢迎。

sentences.en: Of course, everyone preferred the monopolist rule set, because in a board game, being evil is fun.
sentences.zh: 当然，每个人都更喜欢垄断规则，因为在棋盘游戏中，作恶很有趣。

sentences.en: And the landlord's game had a greater capacity for evil than most board games at the time.
sentences.zh: 而且《地主游戏》比当时大多数棋盘游戏具有更大的作恶空间。

sentences.en: If you look at games that are like late, very end of 19th century, early 20th century games, there's not a lot of depth to them.
sentences.zh: 如果你看看19世纪末、20世纪初的游戏，它们并没有太多的深度。

sentences.en: They're mostly games where you're just kind of moving characters along a track, rolling a die.
sentences.zh: 它们大多只是让你沿着轨道移动角色、掷骰子的游戏。

sentences.en: And I think in that context, the landlord's game probably stuck out as something really interesting, weird, different, and innovative.
sentences.zh: 我认为在这种背景下，《地主游戏》可能显得非常有趣、怪异、独特且具有创新性。

sentences.en: The landlord's game made its way around the Northeast to college campuses and activist circles.
sentences.zh: 《地主游戏》在东北部的大学校园和活动家圈子里流传开来。

sentences.en: Folk variations organically popped up in different cities, and properties on the board would be named after real streets and locations.
sentences.zh: 民间变体在不同城市自发出现，棋盘上的房产以真实的街道和地点命名。

sentences.en: And around the time of the Depression, a man named Charles Darrow stumbled upon a version of the landlord's game
sentences.zh: 在大萧条时期前后，一个名叫查尔斯·达罗的人偶然发现了一个版本的《地主游戏》，

sentences.en: that was made in a Quaker community in Atlantic City, New Jersey.
sentences.zh: 它是新泽西州大西洋城的一个贵格会社区制作的。

sentences.en: It featured locations like Marvin Gardens and Vermont Avenue and the boardwalk.
sentences.zh: 它包含了像马文花园、佛蒙特大道和木板路这样的地点。

sentences.en: Darrow basically nabbed the Quaker version of the landlord's game and started to tweak it into a board game that he would sell himself.
sentences.zh: 达罗基本上窃取了贵格会版本的《地主游戏》，并开始对其进行调整，将其变成了一款他自己出售的棋盘游戏。

sentences.en: He called it Monopoly.
sentences.zh: 他称之为《大富翁》。

sentences.en: Darrow, my reporting has yielded that he was in fact unemployed at the time, he was in fact living in the Philadelphia area, and this game made him enormously successful.
sentences.zh: 达罗，我的报道显示他当时确实失业了，他确实住在费城地区，而这款游戏让他获得了巨大的成功。

sentences.en: Darrow made one game a day by hand.
sentences.zh: 达罗每天手工制作一款游戏。

sentences.en: He sold them out of his home for $4 a piece.
sentences.zh: 他以每套4美元的价格在家里卖掉它们。

sentences.en: He used bright, cheap paint, and he misspelled a few of the locations in Atlantic City.
sentences.zh: 他用了明亮、廉价的油漆，还拼错了大西洋城的几个地点。

sentences.en: And yes, he totally stole the concept.
sentences.zh: 是的，他完全窃取了这个概念。

sentences.en: The look of Darrow's game was pretty much the landlord's game, but Darrow improved the graphics and added some color.
sentences.zh: 达罗游戏的外观基本上就是《地主游戏》，但达罗改进了图形并添加了一些颜色。

sentences.en: There's a kind of graphic clarity to Monopoly that's really satisfying.
sentences.zh: 《大富翁》有一种非常令人满意的图形清晰度。

sentences.en: And the game started selling like hotcakes.
sentences.zh: 这款游戏开始像热卖的煎饼一样畅销。

sentences.en: Maybe because it was really fun to handle all of that fake money, especially during the Depression.
sentences.zh: 也许是因为处理那些假钱真的很有趣，尤其是在大萧条时期。

sentences.en: And then Monopoly attracts the attention of a family-owned company called Parker Brothers.
sentences.zh: 然后，《大富翁》引起了一家名为派克兄弟的家族企业的注意。

sentences.en: They buy the Darrow game, and they buy his leftover stock.
sentences.zh: 他们买下了达罗的游戏，并买下了他剩下的库存。

sentences.en: It saves the firm from the brink of destruction.
sentences.zh: 这挽救了公司，使其免于毁灭的边缘。

sentences.en: But Parker Brothers wasn't pleased when they learned that Darrow had not actually invented Monopoly.
sentences.zh: 但当派克兄弟得知达罗实际上并没有发明《大富翁》时，他们并不高兴。

sentences.en: So they start to stamp out all the different versions of Lizzie McGee's game, and finally they buy her patent.
sentences.zh: 所以他们开始清除莉齐·马吉游戏的所有不同版本，最终买下了她的专利。

sentences.en: Lizzie McGee, as best as we know, got $500 for creating, you know, the landlord's game, which I consider to be the foundation of Monopoly.
sentences.zh: 据我们所知，莉齐·马吉因创造了《地主游戏》而获得了500美元，我认为这正是《大富翁》的基础。

sentences.en: Monopoly then becomes the sole property of Parker Brothers, and for years Parker Brothers perpetuates the myth that Darrow just invented the game out of whole cloth.
sentences.zh: 《大富翁》随后成为了派克兄弟的独家财产，多年来，派克兄弟一直宣扬达罗是凭空发明了这款游戏的谎言。

sentences.en: Monopoly made a lot of money for Parker Brothers.
sentences.zh: 《大富翁》为派克兄弟赚了很多钱。

sentences.en: They eventually got acquired by Hasbro.
sentences.zh: 他们最终被孩之宝收购了。

sentences.en: And of course today, Monopoly is everywhere.
sentences.zh: 当然，今天《大富翁》无处不在。

sentences.en: There are hundreds of variations on the game.
sentences.zh: 这款游戏有数百种变体。

sentences.en: International competitions, that McDonald's promotion, and all kinds of shirts and mugs and neckties printed with Monopoly graphics.
sentences.zh: 国际比赛、麦当劳的促销活动，以及各种印有《大富翁》图形的衬衫、马克杯和领带。

sentences.en: But just because people buy it doesn't mean they play it.
sentences.zh: 但仅仅因为人们购买它，并不意味着他们会玩它。

sentences.en: I think that people buy Monopoly not necessarily to play it as a great game, but because it's Monopoly, and it's something you have in your closet,
sentences.zh: 我认为人们购买《大富翁》不一定是为了把它当作一款伟大的游戏来玩，而是因为它就是《大富翁》，它是你衣柜里会有的东西，

sentences.en: and it's something you should have.
sentences.zh: 而且它是你应该拥有的东西。

sentences.en: To me, Monopoly feels like a cheesy Christmas album, like, you know, Bing Crosby or something, where it's not something that you would normally listen to,
sentences.zh: 对我来说，《大富翁》感觉就像一张俗气的圣诞专辑，比如平·克劳斯贝之类的，它不是你平时会听的东西，

sentences.en: but it's kind of something that you might drag out in an ironic way or in a nostalgic way.
sentences.zh: 但它是一种你可能会以讽刺或怀旧的方式拿出来玩的东西。

sentences.en: And that nostalgia feeds itself.
sentences.zh: 而这种怀旧感会自我滋养。

sentences.en: Then you have parents with kids that are getting nostalgic about the games that they played, and they want to introduce those games to their children and play them again.
sentences.zh: 然后，那些对他们玩过的游戏感到怀旧的父母们，想要把这些游戏介绍给他们的孩子，并再次玩它们。

sentences.en: In other words, Monopoly isn't popular because it's a great game.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，《大富翁》受欢迎并不是因为它是一款伟大的游戏。

sentences.en: It's only popular now because it was popular then.
sentences.zh: 它现在受欢迎仅仅是因为它过去很受欢迎。

sentences.en: And we don't even play by the real rules.
sentences.zh: 而且我们甚至不按真正的规则玩。

sentences.en: Well, nobody plays right to begin with.
sentences.zh: 好吧，本来就没人按规则玩。

sentences.en: How many people have actually read the rule set that comes in a commercial Monopoly set?
sentences.zh: 有多少人真正读过商业版《大富翁》里附带的规则书？

sentences.en: For example, the way most people play, if you land on an available property that you don't want to buy or can't afford, nothing happens.
sentences.zh: 例如，大多数人的玩法是，如果你停在一个你不想买或买不起的可用房产上，什么都不会发生。

sentences.en: And that is technically wrong.
sentences.zh: 而这在技术上是错误的。

sentences.en: According to the directions, if you land on an available property that you don't want or can't afford, it gets auctioned off.
sentences.zh: 根据说明书，如果你停在一个你不想买或买不起的可用房产上，它会被拍卖。

sentences.en: This could make the game way more exciting, though not necessarily faster.
sentences.zh: 这可能会让游戏变得更有趣，尽管不一定会更快。

sentences.en: If you can imagine every turn, it's not like a quick decision.
sentences.zh: 如果你能想象每一回合，它不像是一个快速的决定。

sentences.en: Do I buy this or not?
sentences.zh: 我买这个还是不买？

sentences.en: It's like, let's start an auction.
sentences.zh: 它就像是，让我们开始拍卖吧。

sentences.en: What do you think?
sentences.zh: 你怎么看？

sentences.en: Well, let's auction this.
sentences.zh: 好吧，让我们拍卖这个。

sentences.en: And who's going to bid higher?
sentences.zh: 谁会出价更高？

sentences.en: And so it drags out the game.
sentences.zh: 所以它拖慢了游戏进度。

sentences.en: But Eric is reluctant to accuse anyone of playing Monopoly wrong.
sentences.zh: 但埃里克不愿指责任何人玩《大富翁》时作弊。

sentences.en: The way we play Monopoly, even all the cheating that happens.
sentences.zh: 我们玩《大富翁》的方式，甚至包括所有发生的作弊行为。

sentences.en: Monopoly is notorious for people cheating and hiding money and taking money from the bank and things like that.
sentences.zh: 《大富翁》以人们作弊、藏钱、从银行拿钱之类的行为而臭名昭著。

sentences.en: I mean, that is Monopoly, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就是《大富翁》，对吧？

sentences.en: Monopoly is not just a set of rules.
sentences.zh: 《大富翁》不仅仅是一套规则。

sentences.en: Monopoly is all of the cultural meaning and all of the ways that we play it and all of the ways that we use and misuse the game.
sentences.zh: 《大富翁》包含了所有的文化意义，以及我们玩它的方式，还有我们使用和滥用这款游戏的所有方式。

sentences.en: And this is why some game designers defend Monopoly.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么一些游戏设计师会为《大富翁》辩护。

sentences.en: The game designer Richard Garfield, he's a brilliant game designer.
sentences.zh: 游戏设计师理查德·加菲尔德，他是一位才华横溢的游戏设计师。

sentences.en: He invented collectible card games with Magic the Gathering.
sentences.zh: 他发明了集换式卡牌游戏《万智牌》。

sentences.en: I've heard him defend Monopoly and say there's some things about Monopoly that are actually kind of interesting.
sentences.zh: 我曾听他为《大富翁》辩护，说《大富翁》中确实有一些相当有趣的地方。

sentences.en: I was at a convention and came back and my son told me that he had played Monopoly for the first time with his sister and that they really enjoyed the game.
sentences.zh: 我当时在参加一个大会，回来后我儿子告诉我，他第一次和妹妹玩了《大富翁》，他们玩得很开心。

sentences.en: That's the legend himself, Richard Garfield.
sentences.zh: 那就是传奇人物本人，理查德·加菲尔德。

sentences.en: I said, oh, that's great.
sentences.zh: 我说，哦，那太棒了。

sentences.en: How many times did you play and who won?
sentences.zh: 你们玩了几次，谁赢了？

sentences.en: And he looked at me with a strange look in his eye and he said, oh, you don't win Monopoly.
sentences.zh: 他用一种奇怪的眼神看着我，说，哦，玩《大富翁》是不分胜负的。

sentences.en: You just play it.
sentences.zh: 你只是在玩它而已。

sentences.en: But they're not as much about the rank at the end.
sentences.zh: 但对他们来说，最终的排名并不那么重要。

sentences.en: If you're having fun doing the process of play for a lot of kids, that's a game.
sentences.zh: 如果你在玩的过程中感到快乐，对于很多孩子来说，这就是游戏。

sentences.en: So for kids, meaningful play in Monopoly comes when the game is treated less like playing chess and more like playing house.
sentences.zh: 所以对孩子们来说，在《大富翁》中获得有意义的游玩体验，在于把游戏看作是过家家，而不是下棋。

sentences.en: Collecting property is a good thing.
sentences.zh: 收集房产是件好事。

sentences.en: Getting money is a good thing.
sentences.zh: 得到钱是件好事。

sentences.en: Being the Scotty dog is a good thing.
sentences.zh: 当苏格兰梗犬棋子是件好事。

sentences.en: And not going to jail is a good thing.
sentences.zh: 不进监狱是件好事。

sentences.en: But there's not necessarily an end to it all.
sentences.zh: 但这并不一定非要有个终点。

sentences.en: It's just you're following rules and making decisions and accumulating good and bad things.
sentences.zh: 你只是在遵守规则、做出决定，并积累好坏事物。

sentences.en: For me, this was a total revelation.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这完全是一种启示。

sentences.en: I think there may be something to that.
sentences.zh: 我想这或许有些道理。

sentences.en: But I have to say, I played Monopoly for the first time with my boys recently and they were totally in it to win it.
sentences.zh: 但我不得不说，我最近第一次和我的孩子们玩《大富翁》时，他们完全是为了赢而玩。

sentences.en: Carver crushed us all.
sentences.zh: 卡弗把我们都碾压了。

sentences.en: And when we went bankrupt, he would continue to give us little bits of money just so we would stay in the game and he could crush us all over again.
sentences.zh: 当我们破产时，他还会继续给我们一点点钱，好让我们留在游戏中，这样他就能再次把我们碾压一遍。

sentences.en: He was exactly the kind of capitalist that Lizzie McGee was trying to warn us about.
sentences.zh: 他正是莉齐·麦吉试图警告我们的那种资本家。

sentences.en: And he loved it.
sentences.zh: 而且他乐在其中。

sentences.en: My favorite part of Monopoly is taking money from my brother when I made huge hotels.
sentences.zh: 我玩《大富翁》最喜欢的部分，就是当我盖起巨大的酒店时，从我兄弟那里拿钱。

sentences.en: I really like annoying my brother.
sentences.zh: 我真的很喜欢惹我兄弟生气。

sentences.en: 99% Invisible was produced this week by Blake Eskin and Avery Truffleman as The Iron.
sentences.zh: 本周的《99% Invisible》由布莱克·埃斯金和艾弗里·特鲁夫曼制作，他们分别是“铁块”和“铁帽”。

sentences.en: With Sam Greenspan as The Hat, Katie Mingle as The Scotty Dog, and game winner Kurt Kolstad as The Wheelbarrow.
sentences.zh: 萨姆·格林斯潘饰演“帽子”，凯蒂·明格尔饰演“苏格兰梗犬”，游戏获胜者库尔特·科尔斯塔德饰演“独轮车”。

sentences.en: Also playing with Morgan Dewey as my favorite, the race car.
sentences.zh: 还有摩根·杜威，他玩的是我最喜欢的赛车棋子。

sentences.en: Eric Zimmerman co-wrote a handbook on game design called Rules of Play.
sentences.zh: 埃里克·齐默尔曼曾合著过一本名为《游戏规则》的游戏设计手册。

sentences.en: In it, he and Katie Salen tell you pretty much everything you need to design a good game.
sentences.zh: 在书中，他和凯蒂·萨伦几乎告诉了你设计一款好游戏所需的一切。

sentences.en: And you can easily take those tools to design a good anything.
sentences.zh: 你可以轻松地利用这些工具来设计任何好的东西。

sentences.en: Special thanks this week to Emily Kwong and Jesse Fuchs, Matt Forbeck, Sophie Belkin-Sessler, and everyone at the NYU Game Center.
sentences.zh: 本周特别感谢艾米丽·邝、杰西·福克斯、马特·福贝克、索菲·贝尔金-塞斯勒，以及纽约大学游戏中心的所有人。

sentences.en: We are a project of 91.7 KALW in San Francisco and produced out of the offices of ArcSign, an architecture and interiors firm in beautiful downtown Oakland, California.
sentences.zh: 我们是旧金山 91.7 KALW 的一个项目，在加利福尼亚州奥克兰市中心美丽的 ArcSign 建筑与室内设计公司办公室制作。

sentences.en: You can find this show and like the show on Facebook.
sentences.zh: 你可以在 Facebook 上找到并点赞这个节目。

sentences.en: All of us are on Twitter, Instagram, and Spotify.
sentences.zh: 我们所有人都开通了 Twitter、Instagram 和 Spotify。

sentences.en: But to find out more about this story, including cool pictures and links, and listen to all the episodes of 99% Invisible, you must go to 99pi.org.
sentences.zh: 但要了解更多关于这个故事的信息，包括精美的图片和链接，并收听《99% Invisible》的所有剧集，你必须访问 99pi.org。
